attributes.translation: Not only can my boyfriend cook, but he can also do housework, so it is really helpful.
attributes.nuance_translation: A somewhat casual expression used to show that something is not just (A), but also (B).

attributes.body:
だけでなく (an abbreviation of だけではなく) is a common construction in Japanese which translates to 'not only (A), but also (B)'. Sometimes the (B) statement may be left unsaid. This expression may connect to any (A) phrase that だけ would usually be able to connect to.

Caution

The で in では is not the particle で, but the auxiliary verb だ in its conjunctive form. は is regularly dropped from では expressions, or it may also be changed to じゃ, for ease of pronunciation.

The conjunction particle て should follow なく, as it is the conjunctive form of the い-Adjective ない. However, the て in this particular construction is very often omitted.

Caution

In writing, if there is no comma (known as a 読点（とうてん） in Japanese) after なく, the full なくて construction will be required. When a comma is present, both forms are grammatically correct.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: だけでなく vs. だけじゃなくて
だけでなくvs ばかりでなく vs はもちろん

attributes.body: Both add information beyond an initial point, but the nuance differs. にとどまらず means ‘not limited to’ and emphasizes that the scope goes further than expected, often used in formal or written contexts to highlight expansion, as in 影響は国内にとどまらず海外にも及んだ ('The impact extended beyond the country to overseas.'). だけでなく is more neutral and conversational, simply adding another item without emphasizing scale or extension, as in 英語だけでなく日本語も話せる ('He can speak not only English but also Japanese.').

first_relatable.title: にとどまらず
first_relatable.meaning: Not limited to, Not only...but also, Not stopping at

attributes.body: だけでなく and ばかりでなく convey the same essential meaning of 'not only'. Both expressions are often followed by another noun + も, which gives the added meaning of 'not only (A), but also (B)'. The main difference is that ばかりでなく is more formal and appears primarily in written or academic language. In everyday speech, the だけ version is more common, particularly in the variant form だけじゃなくて.

second_relatable.title: ばかりでなく
second_relatable.meaning: Not only…but also, As well as

attributes.body: だけでなく and はもちろん both express non-exclusivity, but differ in nuance and emphasis. だけでなく simply means 'not only (A), but also (B)', e.g. 英語だけでなく、日本語も話せる ('He can speak not only English, but also Japanese.'). In contrast, はもちろん implies the first thing is obvious, while the second is more notable, e.g. 英語はもちろん、日本語も話せる ('He can speak English of course, but also Japanese.').

second_relatable.title: はもちろん
second_relatable.meaning: Not only but also, Let alone, Not to mention, Of course

attributes.body: だけ conveys the meaning of 'only' or 'just'. だけでなく (or variant forms like だけではなく, だけじゃなくて, etc.) is a negation of this, combining だけ with で (the conjuctive form of だ) and なく (the conjunctive form of ない) to express the meaning of ‘not only (A)...but also (B)’. Unlike だけ, だけでなく will always be followed by a continuation of the sentence providing additional information, e.g. バナナだけでなく、リンゴも食べました (‘I ate not only a banana, but also an apple.’).

だけでなく (or だけでなくて, だけじゃなくて, etc.) is a common expression that means 'not only'. It is often followed by another noun + も in the expression だけでなく(て)～も, which has the meaning of 'not only (A), but also (B)', e.g. 肉だけでなく、魚も食べる ('I eat not only meat, but also fish.'). In other words, だけでなく(て)～も is an extension of the だけでなく pattern when you want to specify the additional thing or quality.

second_relatable.title: だけでなく(て)～も
second_relatable.meaning: Not only ~ but ~ also, Not just ~ but ~ also

attributes.body: だけでなく and に限らず both express non-exclusivity, but differ in nuance and formality. だけでなく is a straightforward expression meaning 'not only (A), but also (B)', and is often used in everyday conversation (especially in the variant form だけじゃなくて). In contrast, に限らず has a more formal and academic tone, and carries a slightly different nuance, suggesting that whatever follows is 'not limited to' the thing in question.

second_relatable.title: に限らず
second_relatable.meaning: Not just, Not only… but also

attributes.body: のみならず and だけでなく are essentially synonymous in that they both express non-exclusivity (i.e. 'not only'), but differ in formality. While だけでなく is common in both everyday speech (often appearing as だけじゃなくて) and writing, のみならず is a highly formal expression used primarily in writing and academic contexts. Both phrases are often followed by a noun + も to convey 'not only (A), but also (B)'.

first_relatable.title: のみならず
first_relatable.meaning: Not only...but, Not just...but, What is more

attributes.body: だけでなく and をはじめ both express non-exclusivity, but differ in nuance. だけでなく simply means 'not only (A), but also (B)', e.g. 英語だけでなく、日本語も話せる ('He can speak not only English, but also Japanese.'). In contrast, をはじめ implies that something is the first in a list of many, e.g. 日本語をはじめ、様々な外国語が話せる ('He can speak many foreign languages, starting with Japanese.').
